notes:
Account background: mid-market product analytics SaaS (user-facing playbooks). Evaluating Redwood for inference layer after spike in request volumes — aim to replace self-hosted endpoints for core product flows.

Timeline / recent activities:
- 2026-01-25: Intro discovery call (Alex R.) — high-level requirements captured.
- 2026-02-12: Hosted API demo + cost model walkthrough (Priya N.). Fireflies ff-2026-02-12-0891. Positive feedback on streaming + function calls.
- 2026-02-26: Security sync; asked for VPC/Dedicated options, KMS support, audit logs. Shared security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-03-03: Deep-dive infra call to scope Dedicated POC: canary + fallback routing discussed. Fireflies ff-2026-03-03-1102.

Primary requirements / constraints:
- Workloads: chat support agent (low-latency), doc search (embeddings), reranking for suggestions.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 180ms for chat small requests; acceptable up to 400ms for long context.
- Throughput: ~120 reqs/sec burst, steady 30 rps.
- Cost sensitivity: mid; want predictable unit economics for monthly forecast.
- Data/security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, audit logging, retention controls, EU residency for certain customers.
- Model preferences: prefer open Llama-family variants initially; want fallbacks to smaller quantized variants for cost spikes.

POC scope (agreed):
- 2-week Dedicated POC in US-east region.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool, 95% to hosted for baseline. Monitor latency/cost/perf.
- Fallback routing: policy-based — if Dedicated p95 > 300ms or error rate > 2% then shift to hosted; also automatic fallback to quantized model variant on capacity pressure.
- Region failover: plan to test critical path by simulating us-east outage, expect auto-route to us-west Dedicated region + hosted fallback.
- Rollback plan: immediate traffic cut to hosted api + manual rollback of model config; SE to run rollback playbook (Priya).

Evaluation criteria:
- Meet latency SLOs for chat and embeddings under defined load.
- Cost per 1M tokens vs hosted baseline within 20% savings target.
- Stability: <1% errors during baseline and canary.
- Observability hooks: per-route tracing + token-level cost breakdown required.

Notes from recent meetings / quotes:
- "Wanted something that just works at scale — we can't babysit GPU autoscaling" — Head of Platform.
- Legal wants explicit data residency mapping for EU customers before procurement sign-off.

Action items / next steps:
- RW: send Dedicated POC runbook + canary config template (Alex/Priya) — due 2026-03-13.
- Customer: approve budget cap for POC and start procurement loop; security to confirm VPC peering window.
- Schedule: infra change window 2026-03-22 for VPC peering & initial traffic routing.
- Owner follow-up: Alex to coordinate with procurement and Rosa (CSM) to track contract milestones.

Related artifacts: pricing-proposal-2026-02.pdf (drive), security-faq.docx. Jira tickets: INF-48291 (dedicated pool provisioning), SEC-1102 (KMS integration).

Potential blockers: procurement cap likely requires a revised pricing package; legal wants extra SLA language for region failover. Keep tight on canary observability to expedite sign-off.
